text:
**Review Result**

Quality score: **6.5/10**

The project is small, readable, well-tested for the happy path and documented clearly. I would not approve it as-is because the ingest/update semantics can silently corrupt report data when real-world Slurm snapshots arrive out of order or contain corrected allocation fields.

Tests run: `pytest -q` passed, **61 passed**. `compileall` passed when bytecode cache was redirected to `/tmp`.

**Issues**

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---|---|
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 70-81 | Same-rank terminal states always overwrite existing records, so an older terminal snapshot can replace a newer final state/end/exit code. |
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 74-80 | “Unchanged” detection only compares state/end/elapsed, so corrected user/partition/CPU/GPU/exit-code data is skipped and reports stay stale. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py`, `jobwatch/reports.py` | 118-126, 14/65/115/142 | Offset-aware timestamps are accepted but stored as text and compared lexicographically, which can make report windows and “newest” calculations chronologically wrong. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py`, `jobwatch/reports.py`, `jobwatch/cli.py` | 118-126, 113-133, 181-183 | Jobs with no submit/start/end are ingested but disappear from reports; if all rows lack reference times, `top` reports the database as empty. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 143-164 | Required text fields like user, partition, and exit code are not validated, allowing empty-but-not-null records that degrade grouping/report quality. |
| low | `jobwatch/db.py` | 13-27 | Schema has no indexes for reference-time/report queries, so usage/failure/top reports will degrade on larger accounting dumps. |
| low | `jobwatch/db.py` | 13-27, 52-59 | No schema versioning or migration path, making future active development risky once local databases exist. |
| low | `jobwatch/cli.py`, `jobwatch/db.py` | 121-126, 138-143, 172-180, 52-59 | Report commands create a new empty database for a mistyped `--db` path instead of warning that the requested database does not exist. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **130 lines**.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this as-is.**

issues.description: Same-rank terminal states always overwrite existing records, so older terminal snapshots can replace newer final job data.
Unchanged detection ignores user, partition, CPU, GPU, and exit code corrections, leaving stale report data.
Offset-aware timestamps are accepted but compared as text, producing incorrect chronological filtering and newest-record selection.
Rows with no reference timestamp are ingested but excluded from reports, and all-null databases are reported as empty.
Required text fields are not validated, allowing empty users, partitions, and exit codes into report groupings.
Report-heavy columns and reference-time expressions have no indexes, which will hurt larger SQLite databases.
Schema has no versioning or migration path for future database changes.
Report commands silently create a new empty database when the requested database path does not exist.
